text.name: Financial Management
text.tagline: Control over the organization's cash flow, budgets and costs
text.description: The Cyber ERP Financial Management solution brings together accounting, treasury, fixed asset, budget and cost data in connection with the organization's operations. Automatic voucher generation from related areas, management of receipts and payments, budget credit control and actual cost calculation make it possible to oversee financial resources. Closing the books, preparing the balance sheet and income statement, and calculating financial ratios also support the review of the organization's financial performance.
benefits: Fewer duplicate entries through automatic financial vouchers
Control over receipts, payments and petty cash
Comparison of resource consumption against budgets and credits
Calculation of asset depreciation and actual cost
Performance review with financial statements and ratios

text.name: General Accounting
text.cardText: Record local- and foreign-currency vouchers and review account activity by floating account, cost center and project.
text.tagline: Recording and reviewing financial events at every account level
text.description: The General Accounting system links the chart of accounts and fiscal years to manual and automatic voucher entry. Account coding and floating accounts, batch voucher management, and ledgers and trial balances make it possible to track account activity and balances. Reports can be reviewed by period, account, cost center and project.
benefits: Fewer duplicate entries through automatic vouchers
Account analysis at multiple levels
Tracking of local- and foreign-currency vouchers
Ledgers and trial balances

architecture.title: Strategic goals
items: Optimal allocation of limited economic resources
Accuracy, reliability and compliance with reporting standards

architecture.title: Integration with other subsystems
items: Warehouse and procurement: automatic posting of receipts, issues, inventory adjustments and cost of goods
Sales and revenue: instant revenue recognition, discounts, sales returns and receivables management
Payroll: posting of personnel costs, statutory deductions, insurance and tax liabilities
Fixed assets: automatic depreciation, purchase, disposal and revaluation of assets

architecture.title: Processing and automation
items: Operational events are pulled in online, with no manual re-entry
Accounting vouchers are issued by event-driven rules (rule-based engine)
A real-time snapshot of balances and liquidity

architecture.title: Review, analysis and financial intelligence
items: Multi-level trial balances: reports at group, general ledger, subsidiary and detail (floating/central) levels
Interactive account review: drill down from a trial balance figure to the source document
Matrix analysis: multi-dimensional views (cost center × project × fiscal period)
Financial ratio dashboard: live liquidity, profitability, leverage and activity ratios

stakeholders.text: Decisions based on up-to-date data instead of piled-up periodic reports
Clearer view of return on capital, liquidity risk and financial health
Faster period closing and a transparent audit trail

process.title: Automatic vouchers
details: Vouchers in rials, foreign currency, or both

text.name: Financial Management
text.cardText: Manage period-end operations, prepare financial statements and calculate defined ratios.
text.tagline: Closing the books and analyzing financial performance
text.description: By defining profit-and-loss and balance-sheet accounts, the Financial Management system organizes the closing of temporary and permanent accounts. Generating closing and opening entries, preparing the balance sheet and income statement for any chosen period, and calculating financial ratios provide the information needed to review current and prior-period performance.
benefits: Organized account closing process
Opening and closing entries generated
Balance sheet and income statement preparation
Calculation of the financial ratios your organization needs

text.name: Treasury
text.cardText: Record cash flows, track the status of checks and manage petty cash operations in connection with accounting.
text.tagline: Control over receipts, payments and treasury instruments
text.description: The Treasury system manages banks and cash funds, receipt and payment slips, and the flow of notes receivable and payable. Recording instrument status changes and petty cash operations, and linking treasury operations to accounting vouchers, helps the finance team track funds and commitments in greater detail.
benefits: Status tracking of notes receivable and payable
Receipts and payments recorded by bank and cash fund
Control over petty cash documents and attachments
Treasury operations linked to accounting entries

text.name: Fixed Assets
text.cardText: Record asset profiles, locations and transactions, and calculate asset values and depreciation.
text.description: The Fixed Assets system keeps asset details, groupings, tag numbers and locations alongside depreciation rules. Recording asset transactions and costs that affect asset value helps calculate book value and depreciation. Linking asset accounts to financial operations makes it possible to trace the accounting impact of changes to fixed assets.
benefits: Access to asset profiles and locations
Depreciation calculated according to defined rules
Tracking of asset costs and value changes
Asset transactions linked to accounting

text.name: Consolidated Accounting
text.cardText: Consolidate the financial data of business units and companies and compare their performance in combined reports.
text.tagline: Bringing together company financial data for combined reporting
text.description: The Consolidated Accounting system gathers the financial data of companies and business units using account mapping. Defining reporting periods and checking the consistency of incoming data make it easier to prepare combined reports and compare performance.
benefits: Less manual collection of company data
Harmonized reporting headings
Comparison of unit performance over a common period
Traceability of figures in consolidated reports

text.name: Cost Accounting
text.cardText: Calculate standard and actual costs and show cost allocation details on the product cost card.
text.tagline: Product costing based on materials, labor and overhead
text.description: The Cost Accounting system defines costing periods, cost drivers and allocation bases for service and production centers. Standard costing relies on predetermined rates and planned capacity, while actual costing draws on accounting data and recorded production activity. The product cost card shows the share of materials and operations separately.
benefits: Standard and actual product cost calculation
Transparent allocation bases for labor and overhead
Use of actual accounting and production data
Material and operation shares shown on the product cost card

text.name: Budget & Credits
text.cardText: Budget expenses and revenues and compare operational documents against allocated credits.
text.tagline: Control over credit allocation and budget consumption
text.description: The Budget & Credits system links budget chapters, programs and line items to accounts and organizational units. Allocation, credit commitment and budget transfers, together with control of purchasing, inventory and payroll amounts, make it possible to track resource consumption. Budget performance and variance reports compare actual results with the approved plan.
benefits: Budgeting by unit and heading
Tracking of credit allocations and transfers
Related documents checked against the budget
Analysis of variances from the approved budget

text.name: Revenue
text.cardText: Record revenue items and track invoices and collections in connection with contracts.
text.description: The Revenue system defines revenue sources and items and keeps invoice, receivable and collection information together. Revenue reports by period, customer or contract help track performance.
benefits: Categorization of revenue sources and items
Tracking of invoices and outstanding receivables
Revenue linked to customers and contracts
Revenue comparison across periods
